clue.text: Youngster's an islander

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout, so a youngster
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a child comes from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Cuba, a Caribbean island nation, is an islander by birth.

clue.text: Till the rice grass goes to seed

indicators.note: a plant that goes to seed runs wild and loses its shape, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener lets the rice grass run wild until it seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like 'until' in the surface, but it is the noun: the drawer that takes money in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is the machine in a shop that records sales and holds the takings.

clue.text: Support restaurant in which one has been raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a letter moves it higher up the column, nearer the start of the word

parts.note: a brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone recommends propping up a restaurant where somebody grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the I (Roman numeral one) that moves: in BRASSERIE it shifts up past the E to give BRASSIERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is an undergarment that gives the bust support.

clue.text: Bill died famous

parts.note: a bill is a banknote, a note
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man called Bill has died and is remembered as a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name, but it is paper money.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, a close synonym of famous.

clue.text: Bully gaining a bit of support in flight

indicators.note: the first word gains, taking in the following piece among its letters

parts.note: to bluster is to bully or browbeat someone with loud talk

explanation.surface: A bully gets hold of part of the handrail on a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short posts holding up a stair rail, so one piece of a staircase's support.

clue.text: Almost jeer at para-military group's main predator

indicators.note: almost the whole word, its final letter left off

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player
the UDA is the Ulster Defence Association, a Northern Irish loyalist paramilitary group

explanation.surface: Someone nearly heckles a paramilitary group's chief hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' here means the sea, not chief: the predator lives in the ocean. BARRACK is a British word for jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a fierce, toothy fish that hunts in tropical seas, a predator of the main.

clue.text: Left and right in this country go unnoticed

indicators.note: the left and right letters go inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: the setter is British, so this country is the UK

explanation.surface: Politicians of left and right in Britain escape attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this country' means the setter's own country, the UK, a common Guardian convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurk is to stay hidden, keeping out of sight and attracting no attention.

clue.text: Fool slips up over one fixing on the boards

indicators.note: the reversed run goes over, straddling, the letter for one
in a down clue, up means the fool-and-slips run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool
trips means slips or stumbles
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An idiot stumbles over somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives SPIRTGUM, which 'over' wraps round the I. 'the boards' is the theatre stage, where actors glue on false beards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit gum is the adhesive actors use to stick false beards and moustaches on for stage performances.

clue.text: Apply to take the pee out of pundit

indicators.text: to take the pee out of
indicators.note: the letter P, said as pee, is taken out of the word

parts.note: a pundit is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to mock a television commentator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the pee out of' is British slang for mocking someone; here it means removing the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert force or pressure is to apply it.

clue.text: Erratic and best represented as dotty

indicators.note: the letters are represented in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unreliable who is at their best when acting a little mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is British slang for daft or absent-minded, as is the longer adjective.

clue.text: Our element is providing entertainment for tourists

indicators.note: the letters are used to provide a new word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tour company boasts that its natural environment is laying on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Son et lumiere is a night-time show of light and recorded sound at a historic site, staged for visitors.

clue.text: Praise is Queen's from right that's remaining

indicators.note: the run is read from right to left, so it is turned round

parts.note: laud means praise
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A loyal subject praises whatever belongs to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from right' turns LAUD + IS + ER into RESIDUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual describes what is left over, the remaining part.

clue.text: Writer outlining way to restaurant

indicators.note: the first word outlines, wrapping round, the second

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An author sketches out the route to a place to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author, but it is a pen: BIRO, the British word for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

clue.text: US coach for runner

definitions.meaning: The long-distance bus company in the United States
the racing dog, bred for speed

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to both the American bus line and the fast racing dog.

clue.text: Forerunner of warhorse that's heading off to leap over bunker

indicators.note: the horse straddles the next piece, as in a jump, enclosing it
the word loses its head, the first letter

parts.note: a charger is a horse ridden into battle
a bunker is a storage bin, for coal for example

explanation.surface: A cavalry horse charges ahead and jumps a golf bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunker' suggests golf, but it is a container for fuel: BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a herald or sign of something to come, a forerunner.

clue.text: "Help!" is vocal example; "help over" is analytical conclusion

indicators.note: the song-and-help run is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Help! is a Beatles song, an example of vocal music, so help can also be a song
aid means help
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punning statement that the shout Help! is a song, and help reversed is a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening tells you the Beatles' Help! is a song, so a vocal example; 'over' then turns the run into DIAGNOS before the final pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnosis is the conclusion reached by analysing symptoms or a fault.

clue.text: Goat's first passion might be kid

indicators.note: the first letter of the goat word is taken

parts.note: love is passion

explanation.surface: A goat's earliest love may be a young goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a young goat, which the surface backs up, but it is soft kid leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid glove is made of soft leather from a young goat, so a glove may be kid.

clue.text: At an important point, what Rusedski might want in public hearing

definitions.text: At an important point, what Rusedski might want
definitions.meaning: Greg Rusedski was a British tennis player; at a big point he wants space on the opponent's side to hit into
a court session the public may attend

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis it is the empty space left by an opponent, and in law a hearing open to the public.

clue.text: Deviate from perpendicular

definitions.meaning: to swerve or turn aside, as a ship does from its course
straight up and down, like a vertical cliff face

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to swerve off course; the adjective describes a vertical drop.

clue.text: It's alert when tripped

parts.note: reads like a person being wide awake on drugs, but describes a warning device that rings when someone sets it off

explanation.definitionFit: An alarm bell gives an alert when a burglar or fire trips its switch.

clue.text: Bring about decapitated bird's end

indicators.note: the word has its head, the first letter, cut off

parts.note: a hen is a bird
a tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A grim description of what happens to a bird that loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or make necessary, so to bring about as a consequence.

clue.text: Start of the card game called "cheat"

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken
called means said out loud, so the card game's spoken form gives letters

parts.note: whist is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: The opening of a card game known as Cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIST is spoken 'wist', with no H sound, so that is how its letters are entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist someone is a dated slang term for swindling or cheating them.

clue.text: Cremation's not a bad way to communicate

indicators.note: the letter given by the following word is not part of the rearrangement
a bad version of the word is a jumbled one, so the remaining letters are reordered

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone argues that cremation is not a bad way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A out of CREMATION and rearrange CREMTION to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is a two-way speaker system used to talk between rooms or with a front door.

clue.text: Powder one's bottom to raise applause

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the run is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: talc is talcum powder

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A nurse dusts a baby's rear with powder to earn praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns TALC + E into ECLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, and by extension loud approval.

clue.text: Scottish island doesn't have one large plant

indicators.note: the island's name lacks the letter for one, which is removed

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Hebridean island has no single big plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible: Tiree is famously windswept and almost treeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is a large woody plant with a trunk.

clue.text: Top of Amazon is wet?

parts.note: reads as a question about a river's upper reaches, but a top is a garment and an Amazon is a large woman, so a large woman's top; the phrase is also slang for a weak man

explanation.definitionFit: A British slang phrase for a feeble, cowardly man, a wet in schoolboy slang, worn literally by a tall woman.

clue.text: Those gawping about king being in the altogether

indicators.note: the first word goes about, round, the second

parts.note: starers are people who gawp
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Onlookers are gaping at a monarch who has no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the altogether' is a British idiom for naked; STARKERS is British slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the idiom and the slang word mean completely naked.

clue.text: It backs the tax

indicators.note: the first word is backed, turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something supports the levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like 'supports', but it reverses IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid as a tax to support the church.
